text:
maria_support: heads up — acme-inc (ticket ACME-9321) is seeing function/tool-calling failures right after the redwood-xl-v2 rollout. They get schema errors and the system keeps choosing legacy_payment gateway instead of payment_v3.

maria_support: customer repro (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/call_tool
Authorization: Bearer SECRET
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-xl-v2",
  "input": "Charge $12.50 to card on file",
  "tool_invocation": {
    "name": "process_payment",
    "args": {
      "amount": 12.5
      // missing transactionId provided by caller previously
    }
  }
}
```

maria_support: Response: 400 schema validation failed: missing required property 'transactionId'
maria_support: They also included a sample where the model chose tool 'legacy_payment' even though the app expects 'payment_v3' (we have routing preference by exact tool name).

sam_eng: thanks — can you paste the full request/response headers and the model-assigned tool metadata? is this only for v2 rollout or also observed on v1?

maria_support: only after v2 for this customer. v1 traffic (pinned) works fine. Headers show x-deployed-model: redwood-xl-v2 and x-routing-hash: 0.21. customer says ~18% of their calls now fail.

ingram_prod: deploy_bot shows a gradual canary on 2026-03-10 09:33 UTC — redwood-xl-v2 at 20% global. No config changes to our tool mapping service in that window.

deploy_bot: [deploy] redwood-xl-v2 promoted to canary 20% — build cb3f2a — 2026-03-10T09:33:12Z

john_research: my guess: model v2 changed its implicit prompting/intent signals so the tool selector interprets the prompt differently — it's picking legacy_payment because the new model prefers older naming patterns in the training signal. That would explain both the wrong tool and the missing transactionId in args (model may be dropping fields).

sam_eng: can you reproduce locally by forcing model=v2 and the same prompt + deterministic seed? if model is changing the argument shape we need either a mapping shim or rollback.

maria_support: customer agreed to let us run a repro on their data. they provided a minimal curl we can run against staging with their sample. i'll drop keys to a secure channel.

ops_oncall: quick triage: scope — is this a global regression or limited to customers using tool-based payments? we should check telemetry for function-calling error rate by model version and tool type.

sam_eng: checking logs now — function_call schema failures spiked at canary start. breakdown: 83% of failures on payment-like tool calls; tool-choice mismatch rate up 4.8x for v2 vs v1.

sam_eng: repro steps i ran (staging) — same payload, model=v2, seed fixed: model returned tool name legacy_payment and args omitted transactionId. Repro is deterministic.

sam_eng: raw returned payload snippet (staging):
```json
{
  "tool": "legacy_payment",
  "args": { "amount": 12.5 }
}
```

john_research: ok this is model-behavior, not a routing bug. Options: (A) patch tool-selector to prefer explicit schema-key matches (override model suggestion), (B) add an args-validation auto-fill that injects transactionId from caller when missing, or (C) rollback v2 until we retrain/tune.

maria_support: customer is sensitive — transactions failing is P1. they want either immediate rollback or a hotfix.

sam_eng: quick mitigation we can deploy in ~30m: add a rule in chooser to require canonical tool name map and reject/override legacy_payment -> payment_v3 when schema mismatch. will create a canary rule first.

ingram_prod: be careful — changing chooser logic may affect other customers. suggest scoped rule keyed to customer id or to model version. we can scope to acme-inc for safety.

ops_oncall: agree — scoped rule for acme-inc + model=redwood-xl-v2. also enable auto-reject on missing required fields with clear error so callers can fallback instead of silent failure.

sam_eng: I'll open a quick PR to the routing layer and deploy a scoped rule. if that doesn't restore behavior we rollback v2 for the customer.

maria_support: informed acme-inc of plan. they'll keep traffic on but can accept rollback if mitigation fails.

deploy_bot: [deploy] routing-rule-pr #482 applied to canary for customer acme-inc — 2026-03-10T10:05:02Z

sam_eng: after the scoped rule the staging repro now selects payment_v3 and includes transactionId (we pulled transactionId from the caller context when missing). success on my run.

maria_support: customer reports immediate improvement on canary traffic (failures down from 18% -> 2% for canaried requests). they're monitoring.

john_research: follow-up: we should file an internal issue with model team — behavior shift in v2 causes tool chooser drift. need new evals that check tool-selection stability and arg completeness across rollouts.

ops_oncall: noted. creating postmortem checklist item: (1) add tool-selection regression checks to canary eval, (2) add auto-mitigation patterns (mapping, injection), (3) update rollout playbook for tool-heavy customers.

maria_support: customer happy for now and will confirm after 24h. leaving thread open in case anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:

sam_eng: if the customer confirms green after 24h we'll keep scoped rule and schedule a model-team follow-up. if not, we'll do a full rollback for that customer's traffic.

ops_oncall: tagging for postmortem: @john_research @sam_eng @ingram_prod @maria_support

maria_support: thanks all — will update ticket ACME-9321 with timeline and notes.

maria_support: last update 2026-03-10T10:52Z — customer confirms canary fix holding.
